new_statements.quote: Como hemos dicho, todos los vocabularios que tenemos a nuestra disposición son antiguos y ninguno ha sido establecido según las normas de la fonética moderna. [...] Todo lo referido aquí en cuanto a la fonética y acentuación tiene por consiguiente un carácter hipotético. No es posible establecer una regla general para la acentuación en los idiomas de esta familia, parece probable que el acento tónico racae [sic] sobre la penúltima sílaba y en ciertos casos sobre la última. Resulta también muy difícil decidir si una vocal se [sic] breve o larga. Todos nuestros datos al respecto son dudosos.
new_statements.translation: As we have said, all the vocabularies at our disposal are old and none was recorded according to the norms of modern phonetics. [...] Everything said here about phonetics and accentuation is therefore hypothetical. It is not possible to establish a general rule for accentuation in the languages of this family; it seems probable that the tonic accent falls on the penultimate syllable and in certain cases on the last. It is also very hard to decide whether a vowel is short or long. All our data on this point are doubtful.
new_statements.citation: Loukotka, Čestmír. 1937. La familia lingüística Coroado. Journal de la Société des Américanistes 29(1): 157-214 (section 'Fonética', pp. 161-162).
new_statements.check: not checked by the second reader
new_statements.second_reader_evidence: statement check: group-level-statement. Loukotka speaks of 'los idiomas de esta familia' (Coroado, Puri, Koropo together), calls the accent remarks hypothetical and says no general rule can be set (probably penult, sometimes final). Family-level philological inference from old wordlists, not a Koropo statement; the hedged reading 'unclear' is appropriate. | checker: Loukotka 1937 JSA 29: Gallica ALTO URL (Deb=190) returns 200; held scanned files reopened. The quoted passage stands at printed pp. 161 (last para) - 162 (first para) of the 'Fonetica' section: lines 38-49 and lines 190-202 read 'Como hemos dicho, todos los vocabularios.. son antiguos.. Por consiguiente, es totalmente imposible…
new_statements.relation_note: Vowel and consonant inventories for Coroado, Puri and Koropô (nasal vowels only in Koropô), sound correspondences, then grammatical notes; the accent remark quoted is the only prosodic statement.
new_statements.rule_in_words: For the Coroado family as a whole (Coroado, Puri, Koropó), Loukotka infers from the accent marks in the early-19th-century wordlists that the tonic accent probably falls on the penultimate syllable, in some cases on the final; he states that no general rule can be established and that the claim is hypothetical.
new_statements.exceptions: 'en ciertos casos sobre la última' (in certain cases on the final syllable); vowel length undecidable.
new_statements.identity_note: Treats the 'familia coroado' = Coroado, Puri and Koropô; Koropô sources K1 Eschwege 1818: 165-171, K2 Martius 1867: 167-169, K3 Schott (via Martius). ITEM flags this work read=true, but the earlier reader saw only p. 157 (PDF bot-blocked); the body incl. the Fonética section had never been opened. The accent sentence is stated for 'los idiomas de esta familia' collectively, not for Koropó alone, and is Loukotka's philological inference from the diacritics of the 1815-1818 wordlists, explicitly labelled hypothetical.
